text: Original: INt Jaer ons heren M cccc lxxii tich. Op sinte peeters ende pauwels dach in junio. Begonste suster katherina van ghiseghem profes nonne in onsen cloester te iericho aen dit boec vanden tabernakel te scriuen. Ende sij volyndet int selue iaer iiii dage in april op sinte ambrosius dach. die viel opten sondach. Dit heeftse ter eren gods ende om gemeyn stichtinge met groeter nersticheit bearbeit in allen wtgesochten tijden als sij int gemeyn werck niet sijn en moeste. doense was out xxvi tich iaer. Bidt om die minne gods voer haer ewige salicheit. Dit boec behoert toe. den cloestere van onser lieuer vrouwen rose geplant in iericho. bynnen bruesele bi sinte katherinen. der ordenen sinte augustijns. soe wie dat vint geeft den relygiosen ioffrouwen weder om gods wille. Translation: In the year of our Lord one thousand four hundred seventy-two. On the feast day of Saints Peter and Paul in June, Sister Katherina van Ghiseghem, professed nun in our cloister at Jericho, began to write this book on the tabernacle. And she completed it in the same year, on the fourth day of April, on the feast day of Saint Ambrose, which fell on a Sunday. She did this in honor of God and for the common edification with great diligence, working on it diligently at all chosen times when she was not engaged in communal work. She was twenty-six years old at the time. Pray for her eternal salvation out of love for God. This book belongs to the cloister of Our Lady Rose-planted in Jericho, within Brussels, near Saint Catherine's, of the Augustinian order. Whoever finds it, return it to the religious ladies for the love of God.

text: Original: Hier beghint die prologe op die navolghende sermoenen die welke onse eerwerdige pater her jan storm hevet ghepredict in onsen cloestere te jhericho: doen hi ons commissarijs ende rector tsamen was. welke sermoenen onse werdige mater. doen sij noch inden staet der prelaturen niet en was. aensiende den swaren last ende arbeit des selven Eerbaren vaders crech minne ende devocie dese sermoenen te bescriven: op dat den arbeit des predicaers inder ewiger glorien met nyewen loene vergouden worde soe dicke als yemens devocie beweeght wert. uut aenhoerne oft selve te studeerne dese sermoene. Laet ons ghetrouwelijc bidden voer onsen eerwerdigen pater die den arbeit heeft ghedaen inder predicatien. ende voer onser ghemijnder mater: suster marie van pee god wil haer geven sinen ewegen vree die den arbeit heeft ghedaen om dit te bescriven ... soe hebic dit navolgende boec ghepijnt te vergaderen uut veel collacien die in onsen godshuyse gepredict sijn binnen vijf jaren ...", Dit boeck was volscreven Int jaer ons heren doemen screef.Dusent. vierhondert. seven ende tsestich. des sesten daeghs in septembri. op enen sondach, Hier ynden die sermoenen ons Eerweerdeghen paters welke ic van velen een weynich vergadert hebbe tot mijns selfs orbore ende der gheendere dier in believen sal te studeren Ende sij waren volscreven int jaer ons heren. M. iii[c]. ende lxvi. op sinte laureis des gloriosen maerteleers dach voer vesperen Translation: This book was completed in the year of our Lord when it was written. Fourteen hundred and sixty-seven, on the sixth day of September, on a Sunday., Here end the sermons of our Venerable fathers, which I have gathered a few of for my own edification and for those who wish to study. And they were completed in the year of our Lord, 1366, on the feast of Saint Laurence, the glorious martyr, before vespers., Here begins the prologue to the following sermons, which our venerable father, Master Jan Storm, preached in our convent at Jericho, when he was both our commissary and rector. These sermons our worthy mother—while she was not yet in the office of prioress—out of compassion for the great burden and labor of that honorable father, was moved by love and devotion to have them written down, so that the labor of the preacher might be rewarded in eternal glory with renewed grace each time someone’s devotion is stirred to hear or to study these sermons. Let us therefore devoutly pray for our venerable father, who performed the labor of preaching, and for our worthy mother, Sister Marie van Pee—may God grant her His eternal peace—who undertook the labor of writing this down. … Thus I have taken pains to gather this following book from many sermons that were preached in our house of God over the course of five years.

And it is the eighth that I have copied, all for the spiritual consolation of my sisters in (Christ), and I do not believe I will copy more except for the Corona of the monks, which I have started in another volume. And if the letter is rustic, the author and the words are worthy, and therefore it should be regarded.

text: Original: Questo libro è delle suore e monache del Paradiso. Suor Cleofe., Finissi di scrivere il detto libro negli anni del Signore mille quattrocento novanta Quattro, addì X d’aghosto. text: Original: Di maestro Mariano. Al nome di Dio, a dì 4 di marzo 1488 [1489 in stile comune]. S'io dicho bene, è dono di Dio, s'io dicho [le ultime due parole riscritte] male, son io che o pocha memoria., Al nome di Dio, a dì 4 d'aprile 1484. Questo o ritrato a mia chonsolatione delle prediche di maestro Mariano romano, di quaresima, in Santa Maria del Fiore in Firenze. Se ci fusi manchamento, sarebe mio difetto: non arei tenuto bene a mente. Io Margherita figliuola di meser Tommaso Soderini o scritto questo di mia mano. Chi lo legie prieghi Idio per me. Se gli è scritto bene, è stato dono di Dio e Lui ringratio. Tutto el bene vien da Dio, tutto el male son io Translation: Of Master Mariano. In the name of God, on the 4th day of March 1488 [1489 modern style]. If I speak well, it is a gift of God; if I speak badly, it is I who have little memory., In the name of God, on the 4th day of April 1484. This I have copied for my consolation from the sermons of Master Mariano the Roman, preached during Lent in Santa Maria del Fiore in Florence. If there are errors, it would be my fault: I did not keep them well in memory. I, Margherita, daughter of Messer Tommaso Soderini, wrote this with my own hand. Whoever reads it, pray to God for me. If it is written well, it was a gift of God, and I thank Him. All good comes from God; all evil is from me.

text: Original: f.146v: Explicit exp/iciunt / que cordis intima promunt / scriptando manu /totoque corporis usu / ut clare patebit I oculo quas [ ?) cuncta rimabit / Scripta cum floribus / picturam sie sociamus / omnia hec fecit / et famula sola peregit / in Meding claustro / Luneborch prope situato / ordinis ut fateor / Cisterciensis et utor / Sed si queratur / quod nomen mihi debetur / omnibus et cognita / de Winsen sie vocitata / Elyzabeth proprio / de quo et gloria Christo / anno milleno quadruplex centum addito deno / sexaginta tribus cum quinario sociatus / corporis in festo Christi die venerando / Iubente venerabili domino preposito Tylemanno / de Bauenstede et necessaria ministrando I ob amorem dilecte stte amice Elyzabeth / de Bauenstede Translation: f.146v: "Here ends what the deepest thoughts of the heart reveal, written by hand and with the full use of the body, as will be clearly seen by the eye that examines all. text: Original: f.274v: Hier neempt eijnde dit boeck ghenoempt dat beelt der duechden ghemaeckt (...) duer den subtijlen ende verlichten doctoor bruer peete (sic) dore van Orliens vander predicaren oerdene. The same Reverend Sir himself translated it from French into Dutch, and it was written by me, Sister Marie van der Hochstadt, completed in the month of June in the year 1567, Jesus Maria. Anna.  Flyleaf: For the use of the convent at Cortenberch. (Another contemporary hand)

text: Original: Era ’l sicondo di vespar sonato/ nel glorioso giorno che concepta/ fu l’umil Vergin sancta et benedecta/ per chui ’l primo peccar fu ristorato./ A octo giorni del mese ultimato la faticata penna asciutta et necta/ alquanto riposai et con herecta/ mente l’ora vigesima uscì dallato./ Sonavan gli anni del nostro signore/ cinque cinquanta quattrocento et mille/ quando Maria di Matheo cimatore/ finì copiare el testo et le postille/ di questo clar poeta almo, et de core/ che ’nfino al ciel mandò le sue faville./Laus Deo sit semper benedictus. Praise the Lord, may He always be blessed.

text: Original: A tres excellent Redoubtee & puissant et tres princesse. Ma dame ysabel Royne de France ...- ... Escript le ve jour d'octombre. l'an de grace mil iiij C et/ cinq. text: Original: f.184v-185r: "Completus est iste libellus orarius anno domini M cccc lxxviii ipso die Sancti Ambrosii episcopi. Quem scripsit Soror Wendelmodis Roltemans ad instanciam carissime neptis eius Leve Ter Bruggen honeste matrone. Et Soror Agnes Martini illuminavit. Sancti moniales monasterii ordinis sancti Benedicti ad Sanctam Katharinam In Syloe prope Groenyncgen Urbem inclitam et opulentam in frysia. It was written by Sister Wendelmodis Roltemans at the request of her dear niece Leve Ter Bruggen, an honorable matron. And Sister Agnes Martini illuminated it. The holy nuns of the monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict at Saint Catherine in Syloe, near the renowned and prosperous city of Groningen in Friesland. The aforementioned Leve Ter Bruggen, as a memorable gift, gave this prayer book to the illustrious and honorable man John of the Valley of Roses, also known as Vanden Roesendael."

text: Original: Zu lob und er got dem almachtigen, Marie und allen heiligen und dem menschen zu underweisung, und aus haissen der erwirdigen geistleichen frawn Ludmille, priorin, meiner lieben muetter und frawn, ich swester Barbara, verluepte der regel sand Augustin und der ordnung und statutt Praemonstratensium zu Pernekch, hab geschriben das gegenwuertig puech mit aygner hant, das gemacht und gepredigt hat der hach gelert maister Gorig zu Wien, und ich hab das volentt an dem nagsten tag nach Colomanni des heiligen m[artyre]r. text: Original: f.302: An dem 1316 iar von christes gebort. Is ditz büch erzüget. Von der hoch-geborn vrowen Elzebeten der werden zwire kuninginnen. zu einem ewigen zügnisse iris namen und allers geschlechtes fürsten und kunige om welch closter ditz büch wirt gegeben daz men ir da ewicliche gedenke zum ersten der di da tot sin daz di slafen in Gotes fride und zu der exigen freude kumen. di da noch leben daz sich die freuwen selde und lanklebens; der nach-kümelinge daz si in tusent geslechte wachsen. Amen. Translation: “In the year 1316 after the birth of Christ, this book was produced by the noble lady Elisabeth, descendant of two illustrious queens, as an eternal testament to her name and that of her entire lineage of princes and kings. Whichever monastery receives this book, may she be eternally remembered there. First, for those who are deceased, may they rest in God’s peace and come to eternal joy. For those who are still living, may they enjoy happiness and long life. For their descendants, may they flourish for a thousand generations. Amen.”
